**European Parliament committee backs digital euro negotiating mandate**

*The Economic Affairs Committee's green light clears the digital euro's most significant parliamentary hurdle, setting the stage for trilogue negotiations with the Council.*

The European Parliament's Economic Affairs Committee has approved a negotiating mandate on the digital euro regulation, moving the proposal into trilogue – the final stage of EU legislative negotiation between Parliament, Council and Commission. The vote marks the furthest the digital euro has progressed through the legislative process since the Commission tabled its proposal in June 2023.

The mandate preserves key design features: online instant payments functionality alongside an offline mode offering higher privacy protections akin to cash. Members emphasised the digital euro's role in reducing eurozone dependence on non-European card networks for retail payments, a strategic sovereignty argument that has gained traction since PSD2's limited impact on scheme-level competition.

Trilogue timelines are unpredictable, but the committee vote removes the main parliamentary bottleneck. The Council's general approach, agreed earlier this year, differs on points such as holding limits and merchant acceptance obligations, so substantive negotiation remains. For payments firms, the practical question is when – not whether – the digital euro framework will require integration planning.

*Sources: [European Parliament backs digital euro legislation](https://brusselssignal.eu/2026/06/european-parliament-backs-digital-euro-legislation/) — Brussels Signal | [Digital euro: the Economic Affairs Committee gives the green light to the negotiating mandate](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/digital-euro-green-light-from-the-economic-affairs-committee-for-a-negotiating-mandate-AIvA6gpD) — Il Sole 24 Ore*

**TrueLayer crosses £10 billion in monthly payment volume**

*The open banking payments provider says it processed more than £10 billion in a single month, a milestone that tests whether account-to-account payments are reaching the scale needed to challenge cards in key verticals.*

TrueLayer has announced it processed over £10 billion in payments in a single month, a figure the company describes as a record. The volume is driven primarily by e-commerce, gaming and financial services – sectors where pay-by-bank conversion rates and instant settlement offer a clear value proposition over card rails.

The milestone is worth contextualising. £10 billion monthly puts TrueLayer's annualised throughput in the region of £120 billion, significant for an open banking pure-play but still a fraction of UK card volumes. The more telling metric would be growth rate and merchant retention, neither of which the company disclosed. Still, the number signals that account-to-account payments have moved well beyond pilot stage in certain verticals.

For the broader market, TrueLayer's volume growth arrives as the UK Payments Initiative builds out commercial variable recurring payments infrastructure and Wero scales account-to-account payments across the eurozone. Whether open banking payments can break into everyday retail spending – rather than remaining concentrated in verticals where cards are a poor fit – remains the open question.

*Sources: [TrueLayer Hits Record-Breaking Milestone Processing Over 10 Billion in Payments in a Single Month](https://ffnews.com/news/truelayer-hits-record-breaking-milestone-processing-over-10-billion-in-payments-in-a-single-month) — Fintech Finance News*

**Moneyhub becomes first non-shareholder participant in UK Payments Initiative**

*The data and payments platform's admission to UKPI on a non-shareholder basis opens a new participation model that could broaden the scheme's reach beyond its founding banks and fintechs.*

Moneyhub has joined the UK Payments Initiative as its first non-shareholder participant, a status that gives it a seat at the table for scheme development without requiring an equity stake. The company's initial focus will be on open banking payment use cases in pensions and savings – areas where its existing data aggregation and money management tools already operate.

The non-shareholder model matters for UKPI's trajectory. The scheme launched with nine founding shareholders, predominantly banks and large fintechs. Extending participation to firms like Moneyhub without requiring equity commitment lowers the barrier for specialist providers, particularly those focused on specific verticals rather than general-purpose payments.

UKPI's Wave 1 covers regulated, lower-risk use cases such as sweeping into pensions and savings – precisely the territory where Moneyhub has built its proposition. Moneyhub's involvement could accelerate the development of payment initiation flows tailored to wealth and retirement products, an area where direct debit still dominates and variable recurring payments have yet to gain traction.

*Sources: [Moneyhub joins the UK Payments Initiative](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110211/moneyhub-joins-the-uk-payments-initiative) — Finextra | [Moneyhub joins UKPI as a non-shareholder participant](https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/moneyhub-joins-ukpi-as-first-non-shareholder-participant) — The Paypers*

**Bluecode launches NFC payments on iOS and Android via Discover network**

*The European mobile payment provider's move to NFC contactless, routed through the Discover global network, gives it point-of-sale acceptance at millions of terminals without dependence on Visa or Mastercard rails.*

Bluecode has gone live with NFC payments on both iOS and Android, using the Discover network to route transactions. The integration gives Bluecode access to Discover's global acceptance footprint, enabling contactless payments at terminals across Europe and beyond without relying on Visa or Mastercard infrastructure.

The move addresses Bluecode's longstanding limitation: its QR-code-based payment method, while functional, struggled for acceptance at physical point of sale where NFC tap-to-pay has become the consumer default. NFC capability on both major mobile platforms removes that friction. Routing through Discover rather than the dominant card schemes aligns with broader European efforts to build payment alternatives with less dependence on US-headquartered networks.

Bluecode operates in Austria and Germany, markets where EPI's Wero is also expanding. The two are not direct competitors – Bluecode has positioned itself as complementary infrastructure – but the overlap raises questions about how many European payment alternatives the market can sustain. For merchants, the practical benefit is clear: another NFC-capable payment method that settles via existing terminal infrastructure.

*Sources: [Bluecode brings NFC payments to Android and iOS devices](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110229/bluecode-brings-nfc-payments-to-android-and-ios-devices) — Finextra | [Bluecode launches NFC payments via Discover Network](https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/bluecode-launches-nfc-payments-on-ios-and-android-via-discover-network) — The Paypers*

**Nordic Capital merges Qred and Liberis to build cross-border SME lending platform**

*The private equity firm is combining two portfolio companies – Sweden's Qred and UK-based Liberis – into a single platform for embedded small business financing across Europe.*

Nordic Capital is merging Qred, a Swedish SME lender, with Liberis, a UK-headquartered revenue-based finance provider, to create a combined platform targeting small business financing across multiple European markets. The merged entity will operate under the Qred brand and aims to serve SMEs through both direct lending and embedded finance partnerships with payment processors and platforms.

The combination brings together Qred's direct lending operations in the Nordics with Liberis's embedded finance model, which distributes working capital products through partners such as payment acquirers. The logic is familiar in private equity-backed fintech: consolidate complementary capabilities, expand geographic reach and build scale economics in a fragmented market.

For the payments industry, the deal is relevant because embedded SME lending increasingly sits alongside payment acceptance as a core value proposition for acquirers and platforms. As more payment processors look to monetise their merchant relationships through financial products, the infrastructure to underwrite and distribute those products becomes a competitive differentiator. Nordic Capital's bet is that a single cross-border platform can serve that demand more efficiently than fragmented national providers.

*Sources: [Nordic Capital Unites Qred and Liberis to Create Global SMB Financing Powerhouse](https://thefintechtimes.com/nordic-capital-unites-qred-and-liberis-to-create-global-smb-financing-powerhouse/) — The Fintech Times*
